A Banco do Brasil employee for 40 years, he was CEO of BB Americas from 2023 and previously served as executive vice president at Banco Patagonia from 2019 to 2023 and as managing director of marketing at Banco do Brasil.

mgmt_bio.text: Delano Valentim de Andrade has been chief executive officer of BB Seguridade Participacoes since taking office on August 20, 2025, after the board elected him on August 12 to serve the 2025-2027 term. At Banco Patagonia in Buenos Aires he also sat on the board and the audit committee. He additionally serves as a member of BB Seguridade's board of directors. He holds a business administration degree from Uniao Educacional de Brasilia plus postgraduate business studies.

On governance, Bank of America highlighted leadership turnover, four CEOs in five years, all drawn from Banco do Brasil, and expected no relevant change in strategy or operations; the executive board is elected from among the controlling bank's active employees.

sentences.quote: BB Seguridade has built its equity story around a shareholder-remuneration model that distributes at least 70 percent of annual net profit.
sentences.text: BB Seguridade, the insurance holding of Banco do Brasil, runs a capital-light model that outsources most underwriting risk to its operating subsidiaries, allowing it to sustain high payouts, with a remuneration policy distributing at least 70 percent of annual net profit and an 88 percent payout in the first half of 2026.
Distribution through Banco do Brasil's branch network underpins an exceptionally high return on equity supported by a lean cost structure.
Brasilprev pensions are the growth engine, with reserves reaching 496.5 billion reais, a record level.
High Brazilian rates lift financial results, as net investment income after taxes climbed 16 percent in the first half of 2026.

sentences.quote: Consolidated insurance premiums written expanded while retained claims costs pressed on the combined ratio.
sentences.text: The main drag is underwriting: total premiums written fell 5 percent year over year, with rural insurance, 46.7 percent of premiums, contracting 6.2 percent.
